title: Configurable documenter docs output (solo vs team)
description: Make the per-sprint documenter's output location and git behavior configurable via bober.config.json. Solo users (current default) keep committed docs/sprints/ records for cross-machine sync; teams can keep the repo clean by writing sprint records locally (gitignored) or entirely outside the repo. Resolves the pain that bober silently commits docs/sprints/sprint-spec-*.md into shared repos.

clarificationQuestions.question: Should the default behavior change to not committing docs, or stay as-is (commit) with team mode opt-in?

options.label: A
options.description: Keep default = committed (backward compatible); local/external are opt-in

options.label: B
options.description: Flip default to local (no commit) — breaking change for existing users

clarificationQuestions.recommendation: A — this is a PR into an upstream repo whose maintainer relies on committed docs for a two-machine workflow; a silent default flip would break that. The maintainer can flip the default in review if he wants.

clarificationQuestions.question: What config shape: flat keys on the existing documenter section, or a nested docs object?
clarificationQuestions.recommendation: A — DocumenterSectionSchema (src/config/schema.ts:304) is already flat (timeoutMs, enabled, model, maxTurns); flat keys match section style.

clarificationQuestions.question: In local/external mode, should the documenter still update related repo docs (README, ADRs)?

options.label: A
options.description: No — non-committed modes write ONLY the sprint record; stale repo docs are reported in 'concerns' instead of edited

options.label: B
options.description: Yes — edit repo docs but leave them uncommitted (dirty working tree)

clarificationQuestions.recommendation: A — the whole point of team mode is not to touch the shared repo; leaving a dirty tree after every sprint is worse than committing.

clarificationQuestions.question: Who ensures the gitignore entry in local mode — the LLM subagent or deterministic TS code?

options.label: A
options.description: Deterministic TS helper in runDocumenter before the agent runs (append docsDir to .gitignore if not covered)

options.label: B
options.description: Instruct the LLM documenter to edit .gitignore

clarificationQuestions.recommendation: A — gitignore correctness is a safety property; do it in code, not in a prompt.

resolvedClarifications.answer: A — default stays 'committed'; team behavior is opt-in via docsMode. Evidenced by the Telegram thread: maintainer's solo two-mac workflow depends on committed docs; user's ask is a config knob ('надо кастомизацию конфига допиливать', 'версия bober team — то же самое с другим пресетом').
A — flat docsMode + docsDir on DocumenterSectionSchema.
A — non-committed modes write only the sprint record; stale docs go to 'concerns'.
A — deterministic ensureGitignoreEntry helper in TS.

assumptions: Default docsMode='committed' preserves today's behavior byte-for-byte for existing configs (schema defaults only; no new required keys).
'external' default directory is ~/.bober/docs/<project.name>/sprints when docsDir is unset; docsDir accepts absolute paths and ~ expansion.

The skill-engine flow (skills/bober.sprint, skills/bober.run) mirrors the TS pipeline: the orchestrating agent reads documenter.docsMode/docsDir from bober.config.json and adjusts the documenter prompt.
Scope is the documenter's output only; .bober/ artifacts (specs, contracts, eval-results) commit behavior is unchanged.
This lands as a PR to BOBER3r/agent-bober; no duplicate open/closed PR exists (checked #27-#56: #41/#42 introduced the documenter, none make its output configurable).
outOfScope: Changing the default docsMode away from 'committed' (maintainer's call in PR review)
Configurable commit behavior for .bober/ pipeline artifacts (specs, contracts, handoffs)
A full 'bober team' project preset (presets axis stays nextjs/solidity/etc.); team behavior is documented as a config recipe
Retroactive migration/cleanup of already-committed docs/sprints/ files in downstream repos
Documenter content changes (what the record contains) — only where it goes and whether it is committed

features.title: docsMode + docsDir config keys
features.description: Extend DocumenterSectionSchema with docsMode ('committed'|'local'|'external', default 'committed') and optional docsDir (string). Validated by zod; documented inline like sibling sections.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: When bober.config.json has no documenter section or no docsMode, the resolved config yields docsMode 'committed' and runtime behavior is identical to today.
AC2: When documenter.docsMode is set to an invalid value, config loading fails with a zod validation error naming the key.
AC3: documenter.docsDir accepts a relative path, an absolute path, and a ~-prefixed path.

features.title: Runtime behavior in runDocumenter
features.description: runDocumenter resolves the sprint record path from config and adjusts the agent prompt per mode: committed = today's behavior; local = write to docsDir, no commit, docsDir ensured in .gitignore by deterministic code; external = write outside the repo (default ~/.bober/docs/<project>/sprints), no git operations. Non-committed modes forbid related-doc edits (stale docs reported as concerns).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: When docsMode='committed', the prompt instructs writing to <docsDir or docs/sprints>/<contractId>.md and committing doc files only (current behavior).

AC2: When docsMode='local', the prompt contains no git commit instruction, forbids editing other repo files, and before the agent runs .gitignore contains an entry covering docsDir (added idempotently if missing).

AC3: When docsMode='external' with docsDir unset, the resolved sprintDocPath is an absolute path under the user home at .bober/docs/<project.name>/sprints/<contractId>.md and no git instructions appear in the prompt.
AC4: parseDocumentationResult defaults sprintDocPath to the mode-resolved path, not a hardcoded docs/sprints value.
AC5: A documenter failure in any mode never downgrades the passed sprint (existing advisory guarantee preserved).

features.title: Skill and agent surface sync
features.description: agents/bober-documenter.md, skills/bober.sprint/SKILL.md and skills/bober.run/SKILL.md read documenter.docsMode/docsDir from bober.config.json and pass the resolved path + commit policy into the documenter prompt, instead of hardcoding docs/sprints and 'commit the doc files'. Generated .claude copies stay in sync via npm run update-all.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: skills/bober.sprint/SKILL.md and skills/bober.run/SKILL.md documenter steps instruct reading documenter.docsMode/docsDir from bober.config.json and describe all three modes.
AC2: agents/bober-documenter.md no longer hardcodes committing as unconditional — commit instructions are gated on the mode passed in the prompt.
AC3: npm run update-all --check reports zero drift between canonical files and .claude copies.

features.title: Documentation and changelog
features.description: VISION.md configuration reference and README document the new keys with a solo-vs-team recipe; CHANGELOG records the feature.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: The config reference documents docsMode values with the solo (committed) and team (local/external) recipes.
AC2: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the feature.

features.title: Init flow asks solo vs team
features.description: bober init asks one question — 'Commit sprint docs into the repo (solo) or keep the repo clean (team)?' — and writes documenter.docsMode accordingly.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Init offers a solo/team choice and writes documenter.docsMode 'committed' or 'local' into the generated bober.config.json.
AC2: Non-interactive init (flags/CI) defaults to 'committed' without prompting.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Existing configs (no documenter section, or documenter without the new keys) resolve to today's exact behavior — zero behavior change without opt-in.
nonFunctionalRequirements.verificationMethod: Unit test: parse a config omitting the new keys, assert docsMode='committed' and resolved path docs/sprints/<contractId>.md.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The gitignore mutation is idempotent, appends at most one line, and never rewrites unrelated .gitignore content.
nonFunctionalRequirements.verificationMethod: Unit test: call the helper twice on a fixture .gitignore, assert single entry and untouched existing lines.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Canonical skills/agents and generated .claude copies stay byte-identical.
nonFunctionalRequirements.verificationMethod: Run npm run update-all --check (or the repo's drift check) and assert zero drift.

techNotes.dataModel: Two new keys on the existing documenter config section: docsMode enum (committed|local|external, default committed) and optional docsDir string. Resolution: committed/local → projectRoot-relative (default docs/sprints); external → absolute, default ~/.bober/docs/<project.name>/sprints.
securityConsiderations: Do gitignore mutation in deterministic TS, not via the LLM agent
In non-committed modes the prompt must explicitly forbid git add/commit and repo-file edits
~ expansion and absolute-path handling must not escape into committing files outside the repo
techNotes.existingPatterns: Follow DocumenterSectionSchema comment style (src/config/schema.ts:299-313); path plumbed via sprintDocPath in src/orchestrator/documenter-agent.ts:106; advisory failure handling in src/orchestrator/pipeline.ts:611-618; resilient JSON parsing untouched; utils in src/utils/{git,fs}.ts.

metadata.riskNotes: Additive config keys with a behavior-preserving default; the main risk is prompt-text drift between TS pipeline, agent md, and skill md — covered by the update-all drift check and explicit criteria.
